canonical_statement: For a jointly independent identically distributed sequence of real-valued Bernoulli trials on a probability space, with success probability p identified by the expectation of the reference trial, the empirical frequency converges almost surely to p.
domain_and_universes: universe u; Omega : Type u; MeasurableSpace Omega; probability measure mu; X : Nat -> Omega -> Real; p : Real; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: X 0 is integrable with respect to mu
X is jointly independent via ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X mu
each X i is identically distributed with X 0 under mu
each X i is {0,1}-valued mu-almost everywhere
the expectation integral mu[X 0] equals p
conclusion: For mu-almost every omega, Tendsto (fun n => empiricalFrequency X n omega) atTop (nhds p).
source_boundary: This elaborates the exact strong, almost-sure Bernoulli-frequency reading selected by intake. Primary-source edition, theorem/page, assumptions, and errata remain anchor-audit work; the historical S1_M_263 module receives no statement or proof credit.

killed: changed real-valued observations to natural-valued observations
moved p from a universal binder to an existential conclusion

degenerate_cases: p = 0 and p = 1 remain included. The n = 0 empirical frequency is definitionally the empty sum divided by zero in Real and is proved equal to zero; this single initial value does not change the stated atTop limit. No nondegeneracy assumption is added.
